profile.capacity_note: not published by the operator at the building level. Per CloudHQs own current page for the MCC Campus (tier-1 operator source, https://cloudhq.com/campus/mcc-campus/), this campus is in the Manassas data center market of Northern Virginia, and totals 2,232,875 square feet and 382 MW of total critical IT load across seven data centers, with 96 MW available critical load, MCC5 is site plan approved and MCC7 construction was slated for mid 2025, as of this sessions retrieval. Because this is a seven-building campus total, it is not applied to any individual rows critical_it_mw.
profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 38 (CloudHQ VA missing-address campaign): added a specific aggregator sourced address corroborated by an internally consistent street numbering pattern among neighboring campus buildings from the same source, refreshed company history from the operators own about and founder pages, flagged a second CloudHQ name collision on Wikipedia not present in a prior sessions notes. research_status remains complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CloudHQ, the data center operator, was established in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, per the operators own current about page (cloudhq.com/about/) fetched fresh this session. Fateh previously served as CEO and co-founder of DuPont Fabros Technology, a data center company that sold for 7.8 billion dollars in 2017, and has built and operated more than 700 MW of data center capacity across his career, per CloudHQs own founder page (cloudhq.com/learn-about-our-founder/), also fetched fresh this session. CloudHQ operates as part of the Fateh Family Office, alongside affiliated companies CloudCapital, WindHQ, and Dalian Development, per the operators own about page. The company maintains three regional headquarters, a global headquarters in Washington DC, an EMEA headquarters in London, and an APAC headquarters in Singapore. Per the operators own current about page, CloudHQ now describes 23 global campuses, more than 1,380 MW of contracted critical IT load with more than 6,000 MW of expansion potential, more than 30 million square feet of global data center portfolio, and more than 330 employees. A prior research pass on these rows had already flagged that the domain cloudhq.net resolves to an unrelated Google Workspace and Gmail backup software company, not this data center operator, and correctly redirected to cloudhq.com. This session found a second, separate name collision worth flagging for a future researcher: the Wikipedia article at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CloudHQ describes yet another different, unrelated company, a cloud data synchronization tool for Google Workspace founded in 2011 by Senad Dizdar and based in San Francisco, not this Ashburn and Manassas Virginia data center operator founded by Hossein Fateh. That Wikipedia article was checked this session and found not to apply, so it is not used or cited as a source here, and no Wikipedia sourced company history is included in this reading. This specific row, MCC3, per DataCenterMap, sits at 10740 Airman Avenue, Manassas, Virginia, a street distinct from the LC Campus Loudoun County Parkway and Waxpool Road cluster, consistent with the operators own description of the MCC Campus as a separate site in the Manassas data center market. DataCenterMaps own neighboring listings for this same campus give MCC4 at 10849 Airman Avenue and MCC5 at 10951 Airman Avenue, an internally consistent incrementing pattern along the same street that lends some corroborating confidence to this single sourced figure, though only one aggregator was found giving MCC3 its own specific number.
sources_tried: CloudHQs own about, founder, and MCC Campus pages, a fresh Wikipedia check that found the article describes an unrelated company, and DataCenterMap listings for MCC3 and its MCC4 and MCC5 neighbors

reading.body:
CloudHQ MCC3 in Prince William County, Virginia, is operated by CloudHQ, but no IT capacity in megawatts has been published for this facility.

Without a published capacity figure, the facility cannot be sized against other data centers in this collection, or judged for whether it could plausibly host AI training infrastructure, which typically requires tens of megawatts and up. What is on record is the facility's location and operator, not its scale.

No compliance certifications are published for CloudHQ MCC3. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Virginia has 26 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 20 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 1338.6 MW.
